data_facts_from_extraction: Verdana (plain) and Verdana-Bold: every advance equals VERDANA_WIDTH / VERDANA_BOLD_WIDTH x 2048 exactly; ArialMT and Arial-BoldMT equal ARIAL_WIDTH / ARIAL_BOLD_WIDTH x 2048 exactly (the upright tables are these faces' hmtx).

Verdana-Italic differs from Verdana in 9 code points: A 1398 (1400), D 1568 (1578), V 1398 (1400), W 2028 (2025), g 1273 (1276), k 1202 (1212), m 1993 (1992), v 1210 (1212), y 1210 (1212). Verdana-BoldItalic differs from Verdana-Bold in 2: o 1404 (1406), v 1329 (1331). These reproduce the checker's Java BT 14 pt sums exactly: italic A-M -12 units (119.4717 vs 119.5537), N-Z +1 (130.3477 vs 130.3408), a-m -12 (98.3145 vs 98.3965), n-z -4 (106.0869 vs 106.1143); bold italic n-z -4 (120.3945 vs 120.4219).
Arial-ItalicMT and Arial-BoldItalicMT equal ArialMT / Arial-BoldMT on all 95 code points.

Courier New (4 faces), Menlo (4 faces), Times New Roman (4 faces, pm::times_new_roman_text_width already italic-aware) and Lucida Grande (derived italics keep the upright face) equal what Rust measures through measure_with_family_and_face on every letter, digit and punctuation tested (a lone '`' differs in every family: the public path parses it as creole, the tables themselves agree).

Helvetica-Oblique / BoldOblique equal Helvetica / Helvetica-Bold, so the oblique slots have no upright-table fallback error of their own; Rust's upright Helvetica tables themselves differ from the faces (' 391 vs 455, % 1821 vs 1820, W 1933 vs 1934; bold k 1139 vs 1251, z 1024 vs 1251): that is T14.49, out of scope, reported only.
